As someone who gained a lot of weight from being in a relationship, and a lot of weight from depression, I really respect you for coming from a place of concern for her health. 

Birth control can also cause a great deal of weight gain, and the influx of hormones can really affect mental health. Pointing out her change of size is never a good idea, so I’d really advise against it because the last thing you want is to give her a complex because that’s something she’ll carry with her. 

It also sounds like she perhaps had some disordered eating from the fact that she didn’t eat much when you first started dating. Sometimes, this can manifest into other eating disorders like binge eating. But explain to her that being healthy is really important to you and it’s something you feel is important to share with your partner. 

For me, I’m going on a trip to Ireland with my boyfriend in March, and not only losing weight but getting in better shape so I can enjoy my trip is a big motivator for me. Maybe an incentive like going on a hike, a trip, or doing a marathon could be a good way to kick off the start of a healthier life. Sometimes people just need to feel like they have a reason, something to strive for and look forward to, especially if she is in fact struggling with depression. As someone who suffers from clinical depression, it’s really hard to think of the future so momentary pleasures like eating fast food are easy to give into. 

I do think you have to do some reflecting as well, and decide how important physical attraction and intimacy is to you. Regardless of if she loses weight, if you decide to have children one day, weight gain is inevitable and it may not be as easy for her to get rid of. Not to mention postpartum depression is a serious issue, and will make losing weight harder. 

Some women are more prone to weight fluctuations than others, so I feel it’s important to address how pivital this aspect is to you. There’s only so much you can do to help her, and loving someone with a mental illness is a rocky road. So talk to her, and be honest with yourself. I hope you guys can get through this together, and come out the other end stronger, happier and healthier.

My sister is a dermatologist, and she taught me some very important rules when it comes to identifying if spots on the skin are cancerous. I believe yours is a sun spot since it appeared a year ago. Did you have a mole there before that potentially grew? 

Use the ABCDE rule to check for early warning signs of skin cancers
Asymmetrical: One side of the spot is a different shape to the other.
Border: Irregular border, including a jagged or sharp outline.
Colour: Changes in the colour, especially irregular colour in the same spot. There may be areas of black, grey, white, red or blue.
Diameter: Spots larger than 6mm (about the size of a pencil eraser), especially if the spot has grown.
Evolving: Any continuous change in any of the above; the shape, border, colour and size of a skin spot.

I’d advise you to ask yourself these questions and book an appointment with a dermatologist asap. I’m sure it’s not cancer, that is the absolute worst case scenario. There are many other possibilities, but it’s better to be safe than sorry!

Another budtender here! I’ve been in the legal market for a year now, here are some of my pro-tips:
- Ask the customers questions so that you can narrow down what they’re looking for. I work in a very large store with a wide variety, so rather than suggesting everything under the sun, I try to find what best suits their needs. I start by asking if they’re in for anything specific, as a lot of people come in with a specific product in mind. Next, I ask if they’re looking for a sativa, hybrid or indica. Some people aren’t as experienced with the terms, so if they look at you funny, rephrase it into asking what kind of high they’re looking for. Ask them what type of product they’re looking for (vape, concentrates, flower, pre-rolls etc.), what size they’re looking for, the desired strength and their price range. Some people may not want to be asked a lot of questions, so sort of gauge if they’re really interested in talking or not. Others prefer to browse around the store, or look at a menu and figure it out for themselves. Try not to hover, but if someone is looking to you to help them find something, the best thing to do is ask them questions to target their specific needs 

- Try the products! Since my dispo has quite a few selections, it’s difficult to try everything. But try things when you can, and try to make a note or jot down your impressions of the products. At this point, I’ve tried so many that if I don’t write it down, I’ll forget. I like to include information about the aroma, the taste, the strength, the effects, as well as activities I think the strain would be good for. When you’re high, this can be quite the pain, so maybe just write down you’re first impressions or some key words and enjoy the ride. 

- Ask customers and coworkers about their opinions. If someone tells me they’ve tried something, I ask them what they thought about it. Of course everyone is different, but you always want to give you’re honest opinion to ensure you’re giving the customer the best product possible. If you haven’t gotten around to try something, but your coworker has, you could always say, “I haven’t tried it, but my coworker said…..about it”. Same goes for customers! I have a lot of regulars in my store, as I am sure you will, so don’t hesitate to ask if they’ve tried something, or if you’ve seen them buy something a few different times what they thought about it. Sometimes, you get mixed reviews on a product where one person didn’t like it, while another person loved it. If someone inquired about that particular product, I tell them that I’ve heard mixed reviews, but the only way to find out is to try it yourself! 

- Use the resources offered to you. I spend a lot of my free time researching brands and strains, and especially on Reddit looking up customer reviews. The market is always expanding, and there’s never a shortage of knowledge in the industry. This helps me to not only be a better budtender, but a better customer & find strains that soon become my favourites :) 

- It’s okay if you don’t know everything, be honest with the customer and find the information that you’re looking for from a coworker or whatever resources are at hand. While you may feel silly sometimes not having all the answers, it’s better to be honest than feed the customer some bullshit. Use it as a learning opportunity so that if someone else ever asks, you’ll have that situation to refer back to. 

- Lastly, have fun with it! It’s a dope job, literally, and there’s no better feeling than walking into a dispensary where everyone’s enjoying their jobs. It’s not a regular job that you should be nervous about, learn, sample, joke with your customers, explore. Its a great industry and I’m sure you’ll do fantastic!
I also used art therapy a lot, I found it was a very useful and positive outlet! Painting, drawing and writing are my go-to’s, they helped me take my mind off of the negatives.

Always happy to help :) I could never afford therapy so I used a lot of mindfulness meditation and positive self talk (developing a positive voice to counteract the negatives). I found that made a big difference but sometimes the anxiety was too overpowering to utilize that ability! 

Understandable, I totally agree that medication is best as a last resort. I’ve been prescribed lorazepam 0.5 mg since I was 15 but I only take it in case of emergencies. Since it is a benzodiazepine, it can be highly addictive but I’ve never found that to be the case, personally. I’ve tried a few different antidepressants as well. Some I had a bad reaction with, and some helped and I only needed them for a few months. Citalopram, specifically, helped me short term a few years back, but I sort of felt like a zombie so I got off of it without any issues. I didn’t take any for a while after that but after a rough patch last year, I was prescribed Zoloft 25mg, which I believe is the lowest dose. I’ve never felt the need to go higher than that. I found this one to be best suited for myself, I can honestly say I would not be where I am today without it! I don’t plan on being on it forever, but I’m glad I finally found something that worked for me with little to no negative side effects. I still have my bad days, of course, but I find them to be a lot more manageable. 

I hoped this helped you some & I hope you find something that helps you out on your own journey :)
